findings.evidence: normalise() applies NFKC, which composes base+combining mark into a precomposed letter; _tld_match removes only Mn/Me from the composed text, so the accent survives inside the letter. Sentence 'Claim your energy rebate refund at {X} before the deadline.': X='refunds-portal c\u0323om/claim' -> has_link_or_contact True (no precomposed form exists), but X='refunds-portal c\u0301om/claim' -> False; mask_links leaves it unchanged; SY.verify(sentence+' [1].', [src]) keeps the claim; SY.extractive('energy rebate refund deadline', [src]) keeps the sentence. Also False/kept: 'refunds-portal o\u0300rg/claim', 'refunds-portal ~ s\u0323hop', 'refunds-portal ~ sho\u0301p', 'refunds-portal ~ ca\u0301sh', 'refunds-portal ~ \u0435\u0301\u0444'. surface.build_surface with this text in answer/conflict/title builds (Surface validation via uri_a2ui.validate accepts) and contains 'refunds-portal' 3 times. Probes: /tmp/uri_review_R26/p2.py, p3.py. The _tld_match docstring claims combining marks are ignored, which holds only when no precomposed form exists.
findings.suggested_fix: In _tld_match and _bare, decompose (NFD) each word before removing marks, then recompose or compare against NFC/NFD forms of the list.
